title: Valid Anagram
description: Check if two strings are anagrams using frequency counting, sorting, and optimized single-array techniques.

data.text: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.
An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.

items: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

data.text: Sort both strings and compare character by character. Anagrams will produce identical sorted sequences.

data.title: Sorting O(n log n) — Simple
Analysis
data.text: Sorting dominates the runtime at O(n log n). The `SequenceEqual` comparison is O(n). This is simple but not optimal for large inputs.
Count character frequencies in `s`, then decrement using `t`. If any count goes negative or remains non-zero, they're not anagrams.

data.title: Hash Map O(n) — Optimal
What improved here?
data.text: **Time:** Reduced to O(n) from O(n log n) by replacing sorting with a single-pass hash map. **Space:** O(1) relative to alphabet size (26 lowercase letters), though the dictionary grows with unique characters. This is the standard optimal solution.
Since we know the input is lowercase English letters (26 chars), we can use a plain `int[26]` instead of a dictionary. This avoids dictionary overhead.

data.title: Fixed Array O(n) — Constant Space
Why this is the fastest
data.text: **No dictionary overhead:** Direct array indexing is faster than hash lookups. **Single loop:** We process both strings simultaneously. **Cache-friendly:** The small array stays in CPU cache. This is the best approach when character range is known and small.

cards.title: Fixed Array
cons: Only works for known character range
